PURPOSE: zero-shot classes. Own template plus encoder-decoder generator of virtual questions for unannotated classes, said to relieve imbalance; only before and after figures reported.
PURPOSE: privacy against membership inference. PP-SMOTE adds Laplace noise when placing minority points; classifier AUC and attack accuracy compared with GAN and SVMSMOTE oversampling.
TITLE-ONLY: title names a class-balanced diffusion model with data filtering for fraud detection, read as the paper's own generator; nothing else to check.
Improved SMOTE claimed and designed with CatBoost for NIR origin identification; beats original data and original SMOTE. Change itself not described.
Introduces sc-SynO, a named oversampler for rare cells, but it is based on existing LoRAS with no stated change; compared only with no oversampling. E1 defensible.
EVAL-NOT-STATED: adds latent factors to the GANified-SMOTE architecture as a better oversampler; title says comparative study but abstract reports no data or results.
PURPOSE: generalized zero-shot learning. CEFWGAN adds feedback regulation to a feature-generating network for unseen classes; partly better than the current generative framework on FLO, CUB, SUN.
Outlier detection chained with ADASYN, proposed as Outlier-ADASYN; garbled sentence seems to claim it outdoes traditional oversampling, figures only show with and without oversampling.
One-class SVM joined with SMOTE and random undersampling, claimed as a new distribution-preserving resampling method in the title; said to beat existing methods, which are not named.
CIL: K-means guided undersampling of the majority then plain SMOTE, proposed as the method; compared with existing class-imbalance learning methods on malware and UCI data.
Own generator joining GFlowNet with a variational graph autoencoder to synthesise rare interaction classes; claims better prediction but names no dataset or rival sampler.

Proposed Adaptive Synthetic Oversampling (ASYNO) algorithm in a stream framework with dynamic ensemble selection; compared with existing class-balancing and drift methods. Change from ADASYN not described.

Smoothed bootstrap resampling, FAST feature selection, random undersampling and SMOTE joined in a redefined hybrid approach, in the title; beats an unnamed comparison method, presumably the original hybrid.

Targeted augmentation of minority real-class video samples proposed within a deepfake detector, in the title; compared with baseline and an oversampling setting on Celeb-DF v2. Augmentation operations not described.

DiffusionAAE: own label-guided diffusion plus adversarial autoencoder generating class-specific hyperspectral samples, gains on minority classes; compared with classifiers only, aimed mainly at label scarcity.

PSM-SMOTE: propensity matching, marker selection, then borderline-SMOTE on a marker-based distance matrix, read as a changed neighbor rule; compared only with matching alone. Existing-parts reading gives E1.
TITLE-ONLY: title names WG-SMOTE, a graph-aware safe-seed oversampling framework for imbalanced classification; evaluation and comparison not checkable.
EVAL-NOT-STATED: COSM adds a controller model that rejects doubtful synthetic points from SMOTE or another oversampler; presented as a guideline, no experiment named.

PURPOSE: gender subgroup balance. TransCTGAN adds transformer self-attention to CTGAN generator and discriminator; cirrhosis classifiers judged before and after balancing, CTGAN hybrids explored without reported ranking.
Clustering-based undersampling chained with plain SMOTE, presented as one of the paper's methods; only a high F-measure on two traces is reported, no other sampler.
Two-stage sampling framework in the title: Tomek or ENN overlap removal from the majority, then SWIM-MD generation; outperforms state-of-the-art methods on G-mean over eleven datasets.
Multi-detector outlier removal chained with the existing SMOTE-ENN Bagging method, named in the title; compared only with baseline classifiers without the preprocessing.
CTGSM-DNN: plain CTGAN for rare attack classes then SMOTEENN, named as the proposed system; only its own accuracy on CSE-CIC-IDS2018 is reported, no other sampler.
Comparison of balancing methods on microarray data that includes a novel method sampling both classes; abstract does not say whether it synthesises examples. First check kept.
DAWGAN: a domain adaptive guided WGAN is claimed, but the generation step reads as plain WGAN before SAE and MMD; five comparison methods not said to be samplers. First check kept.
Claims a hierarchical augmentation for class and label imbalance: binary-level SMOTE then a target-group-aware boost, a multi-label scheme; tested on HateMM, no other sampler. Boost step vague.
Web spam framework claims a new preprocessing technique, Split by Over-sampling and Train by Under-fitting; abstract does not say whether it creates synthetic examples. First check kept.

Four existing oversamplers for sediment classes plus a newly proposed class-oriented grouping method; unclear whether grouping changes how oversampling is applied. Only original versus oversampled reported. First check kept.
Own failure-type-aware design, one WGAN-GP generator per failure mechanism, tested against single WGAN-GP, SMOTE, SMOTENC, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN and undersampling on AI4I 2020; result negative.
CWGANGP oversampler in the title, joining WGAN-GP loss with CTGAN normalisation and training-by-sampling; ranked against SMOTE, ADASYN and no oversampling on three tabular datasets.
Cluster-based undersampling chained with plain SMOTE, proposed as a hybrid balancing technique; only the ensemble classifier is compared with other models, no other sampler.
PURPOSE: small and missing data. Own Bayesian-network kernel with derived systems for balancing and over-sampling, tested on multi-class problems; link to minority generation only implied.
SMOTE joined with CTGAN, proposed as the augmentation strategy for slope stability data; only the stacking model's own scores are reported, no other sampler.
TITLE-ONLY: title names a weighted flow matching method guided by data gravity for imbalanced classification, read as the paper's own generator; nothing else to check.
RFCNet balances wafer defect classes with its own autoencoder that adds controlled noise in latent space; only whole-system accuracy against other approaches. If read as a standard autoencoder, E1.
Puts forward a new resampling method named SMOTE-PENN for graded defect classes in a learning-to-rank setting; beats six other resampling algorithms on PROMISE.
IMWMOTE, an improved MWMOTE, in the title and verified on bearing fault data; change not described and ownership only implied. Comparison is of the whole method.
Proposes an enhanced SMOTE with a residual autoencoder and boosting ensemble for cloud IDS on NSL-KDD; enhancement not described, no other sampler reported.
HS-CGK: own DB-CTGAN filters noisy and boundary seeds with DBSCAN before CTGAN generation, then KNN overlap undersampling; beats eight sampling methods on five datasets.
Claims as an innovation SMOTENC with added local density checks on sample quality, inside a stacking model; no sampler comparison. If the check is not a real change, E1.
CNN-GAN hybrid in the title; GAN makes synthetic samples for scarce imbalanced heart data with no stated change or minority targeting; compared only with other classifiers.
IDR_CTGAN proposed as an oversampling technique, described as plain CTGAN trained on the minority class; said to beat previous methods on PROMISE defect data, none named.
EVAL-NOT-STATED: discusses modifications of LN-SMOTE driven by types of minority examples, plus changes to BRACID; reads as a discussion paper, no experiment named.
Hybrid sampling method proposed by joining clustering, oversampling and undersampling algorithms; accuracy and Kappa better than traditional sampling methods on 543 RC column tests.
EVAL-NOT-STATED: WB-SMOTE, a weighted Borderline-SMOTE giving border points more weight than noise points; abstract reports no results, title implies a diabetes test.
GPT-4 used as it is to generate minority-class samples, claimed as part of the framework novelty; only eight classifiers are compared, no other sampler.
Develops a class-conditional hybrid CVAE-WGAN generator with quality filtering and mixing ratios for breast ultrasound; CNN compared with a SMOTE-balanced baseline on BreastMNIST.

Proposes WTASUWO, an improved oversampling joining ReliefF, weighted Tomek links and adaptive semi-unsupervised weighted oversampling; shown only to improve classifiers on imbalanced CFPS health data.
Crash data generation method based on CTGAN (CTGAN-RU), proposed and in the title, no stated change to the generator; beats original data and other resampling methods on Washington crash data.
Guided oversampling and imputation with SMOTE is the title method for Mg alloy process classifiers; how the guidance changes SMOTE is not said, no sampler comparison. First check kept.
TITLE-ONLY: PURPOSE: intersectional fairness. Title names FaireduPlus, using synthetic data to improve fairness of education models; generator and classifier test only implied. First check kept.
Fraud pipeline augments with S-HeMOTE, a heuristic minority oversampler whose name appears coined here; not described and not compared with other samplers. E1 defensible.
Imbalanced deep forest whose units each handle imbalance; abstract never says how, so no basis to tell whether synthetic examples are made. First check relied on outside information.
SCAG-LSTM defect model; its so-called novel hybrid is SMOTE with ENN, the existing SMOTE-ENN, used as preprocessing. Comparisons are with other defect prediction models.
TL-SMOTE re-balancing of client data in federated attack detection is SMOTE oversampling plus Tomek link removal, the existing SMOTE-Tomek; no other sampler reported.
TITLE-ONLY: hemorrhage detection by deep learning using the SMOTE algorithm on imbalanced data, read as plain SMOTE; a deep-learning-based variant cannot be ruled out.

Framework named after latent space oversampling of fused image-text vectors; the oversampler is not identified as new or existing. Compared only with models lacking attention and oversampling. First check kept.
EAINIDS joins SMOTE with cGAN augmentation, named in the title as generative oversampling; ablation only shows augmentation improves the baseline, no other sampler.
TITLE-ONLY: stacking model for electricity theft detection using a hybrid class imbalance technique; reads as an applied existing hybrid, a new one is possible. First check kept.
GANs with no stated change generate synthetic BERT embeddings to augment fake news data, in the title; compared only with models trained without augmentation on LIAR.
AASC: K-Means adaptive sampling chained with SMOTE or ADASYN, proposed and in the title; AASC with SMOTE best among other sampling techniques on dental cavity images.
Hybrid sampling technique proposed as complementary fuzzy SVM followed by plain SMOTE; compared only with other fuzzy SVM classifiers on four benchmarks and plant cell data, no other sampler.
SMOTE-PCA-HDBSCAN framework in the title: SMOTE, PCA, then HDBSCAN removal of noisy synthetic points; compared with SMOTE, SMOTE-DBSCAN, SMOTE-ENN and SMOTE-Tomek on water quality data.
HRBwSD, an own hybrid algorithm built on radial-based oversampling and undersampling with duplicate exclusion; results comparable to other class balancing algorithms. Data not named.
SMSN model named for stacking and a modified SMOTE, but the abstract says the modified SMOTE was adopted and does not describe it; no sampler comparison. First check kept.
SMOTERN removes noisy minority seeds by neighbor count before SMOTE generation; AUC and F2 better than other methods on OULAD. DOCTYPE: chapter
Credit risk warning model that introduces an enhanced SMOTE before CNN features and PSO-tuned ELM; enhancement not described, only whole-model accuracy gain reported.
ADASYN chained with NCL cleaning, then an AdaBoost SVM ensemble, proposed as integrated hybrid sampling; abstract only claims certain advantages on 10 KEEL sets, no rival sampler named.
Botshot: vanilla and conditional GANs used as they are to generate botnet traffic for scarce imbalanced data and evasion hardening; compared with benchmark oversampling methods over six classifiers.

Introduces several SMOTE extensions (Distance and Dirichlet ExtSMOTE, FCRP-SMOTE, BGMM-SMOTE, DeepExt-SMOTE) using weighted neighbor averages, validated empirically; rival samplers not named. DOCTYPE: thesis
AdaptiveSMOTE-RF: SMOTE with adaptively set sampling ratio plus random forest feature selection and weighted trees; better than the original algorithm on Kaggle data. Adaptive-SMOTE may be existing.
Vague pipeline joining downsampling and oversampling before logistic regression and random forest; no resampling step is named or described as new. First check kept.
Conditional GAN with no stated change generates minority samples inside split federated learning, in the title; only one accuracy figure, no other sampler. If read as built into training, include.
KSIPF in the title: k-means SMOTE followed by iterative-partitioning filter noise removal; compared with SMOTE and its variants on 30 synthetic and 20 real datasets.
Unrolled GAN used as the oversampler for credit card fraud with no stated change, in the title; contrasted with traditional oversampling methods.

Comparative churn study with SMOTE and ADASYN that also tests a novel two-phase clustering and ensemble resampling with LSTM; unclear if it synthesises examples. First check kept, E-COMPARE defensible.
Two-step method in the title: mutual-information-based downsampling then plain SMOTE for sepsis prediction; only a challenge utility score and cross-validation reported, no other sampler.
Lithology framework claims an adaptive resampling mechanism joining dynamic balanced group instance selection with an optimized SMOTE; change not described, compared only with traditional learners.
SyntheticAug, a Gaussian copula augmentation with no stated change, named and in the title; beats SMOTE-NC and the baseline on 176 NAFLD patients.
GAN with no stated change proposed to balance three datasets, in the title; decision tree accuracy reported only before and after augmentation.
Malware image classifier with autoencoder generator introduces a self-adjustive oversampling technique for minority classes; how samples are made is not described, no sampler comparison.
PSO-based oversampling of the minority class for card fraud, compared with a GA-based one using random forest; generation mechanism not detailed.
FedBIP lists a segmentation-based oversampling method as a component, checked by ablation; abstract does not say whether it is new or makes synthetic samples. First check kept.
EVAL-NOT-STATED: COSMOTE, a resampling technique using ordinal class information to create minority defect images; workflow outlined, no results reported.
SAGA joins SMOTE with a feature-space-partitioning ensemble tuned by genetic algorithm; unclear whether SMOTE is built into the ensemble or plain preprocessing. First check kept, E1 defensible.

PURPOSE: fairness. Own demographic-conditioned diffusion framework augments hard samples and filters poor synthetics; classifier beats state-of-the-art methods on Harvard-FairVLMed, rivals not named as samplers.
Rough set theory joined with SMOTE as the paper's preprocessing approach, in the title; compared with various preprocessing techniques on six datasets and three classifiers.
AGM sampling joins ADASYN with GMM clustering, named as a novel strategy; results only compare the C3BANet detector with leading algorithms, no other sampler.
Undescribed modified SMOTE incorporated in preprocessing for a tumor segmentation U-Net; not clear it is the paper's own, comparisons concern segmentation models. First check kept.
ISCOTE oversampler with adaptive scaling inside SVC layers, for tool life regression recast as imbalanced multi-class classification; compared with SMOTE and MWMOTE on two datasets.
Proposes a modified conditional WGAN-GP generating hyperspectral data cubes for scarce, imbalanced classes; judged by spectral similarity and classification outcomes. DOCTYPE: chapter
HAR-MI joined with hybrid sampling steps (MOSHS, Different Contribution Sampling) for multi-class imbalance and overlap, in the title; compared with neighbourhood-based undersampling.
Balancing method based on SMOTE and KNN is called proposed but reads as standard SMOTE preprocessing; no sampler comparison, contribution is failure mode and fragility modelling. First check kept.
DK-MS in the title: double K-means data reduction chained with plain SMOTE; compared only with cases without balancing, over four classifiers.
TriBal in the title: SMOTE, then Cluster Centroids, then ENN as a three-level framework; said to beat existing sampling techniques on nine benchmark datasets.
K-means downsampling chained with ACGAN oversampling plus improved one-vs-all training on NSL-KDD; compared only as a whole with state-of-the-art methods, no other sampler named.
TITLE-ONLY: title names an adaptive kernel SMOTE-SVM algorithm for imbalanced classification, read as a new SMOTE variant coupled with SVM; nothing else to check.
TabDDPM with a dual-consistency filter generates minority samples; filter looks custom but the abstract says employed, so own or existing-parts is unclear. First check kept, E1 defensible.
SMOTE plus class-specific autoencoder reconstructions as the augmentation part of the HEART ensemble; only classifiers are compared, no other resampler.
GMBoost is a geometric-mean boosting algorithm; over-sampling is named only in the title and not described; compared with AdaBoost and cost-sensitive boosting, not with resamplers.
TITLE-ONLY: GAN-augmented gradient boosting framework under class imbalance; cannot tell if the GAN is own or standard, nor any comparison; continuous prediction may be regression.
OOG, a named GAN sampling technique with Optuna-chosen variant and settings, claimed as the method for imbalanced malware data; compared with SMOTE.
HyRes-Boost chains ADASYN then ENN with XGBoost, named in title; abstract reports results only against the unbalanced baseline, no other resampler named.
Conditional GAN claimed as the newly proposed model to generate minority feature data for hardware Trojan detection; compared with original data and with SMOTE-balanced data.
BDT combines under-sampling, over-sampling and algorithmic adjustment as the named technique; beats established methods on several datasets; abstract does not say the oversampling is synthetic.
SHDO chains SMOTE, random oversampling, SVMSMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and SMOTEN in sequence as the proposed approach; outperforms other oversamplers, SVMSMOTE second. DOCTYPE: chapter
KSMOTEEN joins K-means clustering with SMOTE-ENN as the named hybrid sampling model; reported to outperform some existing sampling methods.
Claims an improved SMOTE: CVCF noise filter before SMOTE, with PSO-tuned SVM; compared only with other advanced algorithms. If read as existing parts chained, no resampler comparison is stated.
Proposes extending SMOTE with the Iterative-Partitioning Filter for noisy and borderline examples; compared with SMOTE and its well-known generalizations.
Osteosarcoma CNN paper says an oversampling technique is proposed but does not describe it; may be duplication or standard augmentation; only balanced versus imbalanced training compared.
Framework applies SMOTE hierarchically to balance several question types in grammar-based question classification; experiments reported, no comparison with other resamplers stated.
TITLE-ONLY: traffic sign classification based on minority oversampling and CNN; title does not claim a new oversampler and nothing shows how it is done or compared.
EVAL-NOT-STATED: ASMOTE-TDC module, time-aware oversampling with Beta interpolation and Fourier correction, is the paper's own part of a credit default ensemble; no data or comparison reported.

PURPOSE: fairness. FedIDA pairs fairness regularization with group-conditional oversampling in federated learning; abstract does not say the oversampling is synthetic or compare it with other resamplers.

Thesis designs its own AI-enhanced synthesis algorithm mixing GAN and formula-based generation for minority classes; SMOTE and GAN studied in other chapters, no direct comparison stated. DOCTYPE: thesis
SMOTE plus Gaussian noise augmentation named in title as part of CIN-RiskNet; only ablations and classifier comparisons reported, no other resampler.
Drift-adaptive stream method with ensemble-based resampling that oversamples minority instances; not stated whether synthetic or replicated; compared with unnamed baseline techniques.

Label Correlation Guided Borderline Oversampling is an existing named method used to balance images; contribution is the optimized WDCGAN classifier; compared only with other classifiers. Wording says introduced.
Intrusion detector joining DNN, GAN and feature selection on KDD99; SMOTE only mentioned as a common oversampler, GAN role not stated, no results or resampler comparison.
FEDGAN-IDS, a federated BiGAN tuned by bee-colony optimization, generates synthetic minority-class samples for intrusion detection; compared with other IDS models, not with other resamplers.

HSMOTE introduced as the paper's oversampler, interpolating between close minority instances, inside a feature selection and ensemble framework; tested on various datasets, no resampler comparison stated.
Introduced balancing chain of Tomek links, Borderline-SMOTE and a pruning step in federated fraud detection; compared only with traditional models. Pruning step may be the paper's own.
Proposes an adaptive sampling strategy combining oversampling and undersampling for DDoS classification; compared with baselines and conventional sampling methods; synthetic generation not stated.
Novel preprocessing technique: SMOTE then cluster-based majority undersampling sized to the new minority count; better than previous approaches on 10 datasets, though those are not named.
Proposed oversampling technique: WGAN-GP generates attack samples, then ANOVA feature selection; outperforms the baselines on three intrusion sets, baselines not named after a survey of oversamplers.

EVAL-NOT-STATED: introduces own enhanced oversampling techniques (MEMMOT, MMMm, NFN-M, CME and others) for multiclass big data; experiments and comparison with prior work only planned. DOCTYPE: chapter
DTW-SMOTE with adaptive sampling and dynamic denoising is a component of the proposed water quality network; novelty of the variant not stated; only baseline models compared.
Digital twin attack detection with LSTM and standard SMOTE plus silhouette-based removal of between-cluster samples; resampling is a supporting step and is not compared with other resamplers.
Hybrid of SMOTE and Neighborhood Cleaning Rule proposed for credit card fraud; only balanced versus original data is compared, with logistic regression.

BE-DTI bagging ensemble with active learning and dimensionality reduction for drug-target prediction; oversampling inside the bagging is not described; compared with five competing techniques, not resamplers.
Proposes hybrid balancing techniques that generate minority data for tabular and image sets; outperform state-of-the-art techniques on Pima, stroke, MNIST and Fashion-MNIST; generation not described.
Two-phase strategy applying oversampling, undersampling and hybrid steps in sequence for click fraud; no comparison with other resamplers reported and synthetic generation not stated.
BOO-ST is boosting with SMOTE and Tomek links, that is SMOTE-Tomek with a boosting classifier; no change to the sampler described and no resampler comparison reported.
Electricity theft framework; SMOTE followed by an unnamed post-balancing noise reduction step is preprocessing; contribution is the DTRF ensemble with firefly tuning and XAI.
Graph IDS includes Attention-Weighted Graph Synthetic Oversampling, a name not known as an existing method, within the proposed system; compared only with ML and DL classifiers.

Own augmentation with a generative stage simulating synthetic defects and Siamese validation to balance minority defect classes; compared with baseline augmentation approaches; task is semantic segmentation.
Framework combines finite element-based SMOTE (FE-SMOTE) with stochastic cross validation and a new tuning rule; abstract does not say whether FE-SMOTE is introduced here; no resampler comparison.
D-ENN combines the existing DEBOHID oversampler with ENN as a novel hybrid; beats nine state-of-the-art sampling methods on 44 datasets.
Geo-WGAN, a named multi-source geoscientific WGAN, generates synthetic ore-bearing samples before a biased SVM and CNN for prospectivity mapping; no comparison with other generators stated.

Novel hybrid sampling: random undersampling plus a conditional WGAN with special generator and discriminator structures for mixed variables; superior to all benchmark methods on Kaggle backorder data.
COSDF builds SMOTE into co-training with density-based filtering of noisy synthetic and newly labeled instances; best among compared methods on six defect datasets, methods not named.
SAKOS chains SMOTE, All-KNN, One-Sided Selection and a final SMOTE as the proposed framework; only gains in classification metrics reported, no other resampler named.
WCGAN with gradient penalty, an existing generator, synthesizes minority traffic samples, plus modified PSO feature selection; compared only with other detection approaches on UNSW-NB15.
Intrusion detection CNN on image-converted data; an unspecified oversampling method is used as a balancing step and not claimed as new; only competing algorithms compared.
Protein localization method with Radius-SMOTE in the title; abstract says it is used and does not say whether it is introduced here; compared with other conventional methods only.

Composite-kernel SVM for hierarchical multi-label gene function prediction introduces a supervised clustering with over-sampling strategy; not stated whether samples are synthetic; no resampler comparison.
Combines an unspecified over- plus under-sampling technique with twin SVM; no own sampler claimed, synthetic generation not stated, and only other state-of-the-art methods compared.
SMOTE-based informed sampling with a post-classification adaptive weighting; no change to SMOTE described, the new part is the weighting; traffic offence case study, no results or comparison stated.

Standard SMOTE applied to training data, then Rotation Forest as the classifier; compared with SMOTE-Boost, SMOTE-Bagging and SMOTE-random subspace. Called a new ensemble method, but the sampler is unchanged.
Proposes a combined algorithm of farther-distance SMOTE (FD_SMOTE) and PCA for medical data; FD_SMOTE is not a known existing method; evaluated by accuracy and AUC, no resampler comparison.
Adaptive Data Boosting algorithm incrementally reinforces a target user set with other users speech and then SMOTE-based augmentation; tested on IEMOCAP, no comparison with other resamplers stated.
IoT attack detection framework with a customized, adaptive SMOTE named in the title; the change to SMOTE is not described; evaluated on RT-IoT2022 without resampler comparison.
TBSSVM chains Tomek links with Borderline-SMOTE SVM as one of two novel methods; baselines reported are classifiers only, no other resampler compared.
Federated IDS with client-side SMOTE (CSMOTE) and federated cost-sensitive learning, applying SMOTE inside federated training; outperforms unnamed baselines; CSMOTE detail not given.
SMOTEOSS, SMOTE followed by one-sided selection, designed as a new hybrid sampler; validated against 10 state-of-the-art sampling methods on click fraud and 10 benchmark sets.
CGAN-based oversampling, joined with reinforcement learning in the proposed solution and named in the title; reported better than SMOTE and ADASYN on four classifiers.
Mixture of experts with a DNN-based SMOTE generating synthetic fraud samples, claimed as a novel approach; DNN-SMOTE may pre-exist; no comparison with other resamplers stated.
PURPOSE: fairness. PC-SMOTE and PC-ADASYN oversample protected subcategories instead of class labels; decision trees evaluated for accuracy, F1 and fairness; no outside resampler comparison stated.
Healthcare RNN pipeline claims an Improved SMOTE balancing step among its own improved components; the change is not described; only classifiers are compared.
Lamont reduces the coverage matrix with a revised LDA and then uses standard SMOTE to synthesize failing tests; compared with the augmentation method Aeneas; downstream task is statement ranking.
ESBagging: ENN cleaning, then SMOTE, then bagging, proposed as the algorithm; compared with BalancedBagging and SMOTEBagging on 10 KEEL sets.
Mixed sampling of an improved SMOTE with Tomek links plus weighted-vote random forest; SMOTE change not detailed; verified on UCI data without a stated resampler comparison.

PURPOSE: privacy. Adapts oversampling, SMOTE and synthetic data generation to differential privacy as pre-processing for class imbalance; the private variants are compared with each other and with weighting.
KNN air quality classifier with standard SMOTE and multi-verse optimization for parameter tuning; no change to SMOTE described and no resampler comparison.
SMOTE plus CTGAN augmentation named in the title of an intrusion detection framework; all results concern the Bi-LSTM and VAE detector, no other resampler compared.
Designs an oversampling algorithm coupling Top-N reverse kNN with SMOTE; tested on UCI sets with four classifiers and four distance metrics; no other resampler compared.
Pneumonia framework whose stated novelty is imbalance handling: DCGAN with WGAN-GP for the minority class plus random undersampling; parts are existing and no other resampler is compared.
Borderline-SMOTE used with stacking, bagging and boosting on seven multiclass KEEL sets; only the three pairings are compared; not stated that the sampler is built into the ensembles.
Semiconductor fault detection paper proposes its own over-sampling technique for rare fail cases with feature selection; technique not described and may be duplication; no resampler comparison.
Standard mixup used for minority-class balancing, named in the title; contribution and all comparisons concern the CNN graph-attention classifier.
FHR-KNN joins feature selection, a hybrid resampling technique and KNN; resampler not described; reports higher accuracy than the traditional oversampling technique on preeclampsia data.
PURPOSE: fairness. Proposes balancing methods using generative AI fake data for protected groups, set against SMOTE as baseline; classifiers benchmarked on German credit and Berkeley admission data.

Imbalanced sentiment method with context lexicon, BiLSTM and a text-based sampling step that generates new text samples; garbled abstract, sampler novelty unclear; compared with deep model benchmarks only.
Horoscope-based profession prediction combining a Randomized Weighted SMOTE with standard classifiers; variant not claimed as new, no evaluation or comparison described; could be an own variant.
Proposes a heterogeneous ensemble learning method built on EasyEnsemble and SMOTE for ship classification; compared with homogeneous ensembles and the same ensemble without SMOTE.
WSN intrusion pipeline with a correlation-coefficient-centered SMOTE (CC-SMOTE) among its modified components; the change is not described and no resampler comparison is reported.
DBSCAN plus SMOTE before an LSTM, named in the title; only LSTM with versus without DBSCAN and SMOTE is compared on DDoS data.
Bias-aware hybrid sampling joins SMOTE-Tomek and ADASYN with demographic tracking; unclear whether tracking changes generation or the parts are used as is; compared only with transformers.
EVAL-NOT-STATED: proposes DeepSMOTE, SMOTE-based oversampling in an encoder/decoder latent space with a penalized loss for minority images; abstract reports no experiments or result comparison.
SMOTE-PCADBSCAN chains SMOTE, PCA and DBSCAN removal of poor points as a novel model, named in the title; compared with original data, SMOTE and SMOTE-DBSCAN on water quality data.

Mostly a comparison of imbalance techniques for mammography, but includes the authors own synthetic lesion generation, which beats class weighting, over-sampling and under-sampling; may be introduced elsewhere.
SMOTERN, SMOTE combined with noise removal, introduced as the balancing method for a mixture-of-experts student model; no comparison with other resamplers reported in the abstract.
GenOMe, a named generative oversampler drawing points under Beta, Gamma or Gaussian constraints, on apnea ECG data; outperforms original data and SMOTE. Wording says employed.
AdaBoost enhancement using a Heron-Centroid SMOTE with capping and early stopping; abstract does not say whether that variant is new; only before and after figures given.

PURPOSE: imputation and data simulation. ModGraProDep graphical-model generator simulates synthetic data for small imbalanced patient subsets; compared with oversampling algorithms on two cancer registries; classifier use only implied.
COU model: existing RSMOTE oversampling followed by ENN, named in the title; F-measure 11 percent above RSMOTE alone on software defect data.

PURPOSE: fairness. Abstract says it introduces FAWOS, synthesizing points for hard cases in sensitive-attribute neighborhoods; FAWOS is an earlier published method, so originality needs checking; no resampler comparison.
TITLE-ONLY: title claims a new hybrid sampling method for imbalanced classification with ensemble decision trees; synthetic generation and any comparison cannot be confirmed.
EVAL-NOT-STATED: proposes SMOTEWB, boosting-based noise detection that sets the number of neighbors per observation inside SMOTE; abstract names no experiments or comparison.
BDSK combines SMOTE with K-means-based undersampling, named in the title; tested on the Tan text corpus with no stated comparison against other resamplers.
Hybrid resampling of k-means clustering then ADASYN before random forest, named in the title; outperforms ADASYN-RF, RF and XGBoost on coal logging data.
Proposes sampling with reference to SVM support vectors instead of all training data for imbalanced hyperspectral classes; synthetic generation not confirmed; no resampler comparison stated.
SHDO applies five existing oversamplers in sequence, named in the title; only an ablation with and without SHDO is reported. Same scheme as R18367, which did compare with other oversamplers.
TITLE-ONLY: title announces an innovative oversampling approach using functional data analysis for imbalanced classification; no abstract, so no comparison known.
Study of Bayesian network classifiers on 129 imbalanced sets; adds minority oversampling to a target imbalance ratio, kind of oversampling not stated, could be plain duplication.
SMOTE-NCL, SMOTE with a neighborhood cleaning filter, proposed and named in the title; reported better than the existing SMOTE method on KDDCUP 99.
Proposes hybrid K-Means SMOTE plus ENN; best against the imbalanced data and other resamplers (SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, Tomek, ENN, SMOTE-Tomek, SMOTE-ENN) on diabetes data.
Claims an improved SMOTE based on PCA, noise and dimension reduction before interpolation, with random forest; tested on internet finance firms; garbled abstract, no resampler comparison.
USMOTE is random undersampling chained with plain SMOTE, named in title; abstract reports better recall but names no other resampler as comparison. Coined name could be read as own claim.

GAN oversampling for turnover data with a claimed two-step refining of generated data to keep minority-class rows; GAN-balanced data beats SMOTE-balanced and original data. Largely applied study.

SMOTE sampling built into the online SAM-kNN learner for drifting streams; paper also proposes Informed Downsampling (no synthetic), which is reported as the better variant.
Coins DCGAN-SMOTE, a conditional GAN coupled with k-means-guided SMOTE interpolation, as its balancer; only ablations reported. If read as existing parts chained, this would be E1.
NMOTe, a new minority oversampling algorithm for binary imbalance; mechanism not described; claimed to beat existing state-of-the-art techniques on standard datasets.
KNN plus Jaccard similarity synthetic minority resampling with drift detection for streams; said to outperform existing over- and undersampling. Preprint.
BSCGAN, structured conditional GAN oversampling in a VAE latent space with balanced pretraining; compared with state-of-the-art methods such as GAMO and DeepSMOTE on four image sets.
Overview of credit card fraud methods plus SVM and logistic regression with unspecified imbalance handling; no resampling method of its own stated.
Contribution is transaction graph construction; existing GraphSMOTE integrated, with edges of synthetic nodes set by the same similarity rule. Could be read as a changed application. Borderline.
FEM-constrained improved elliptical SMOTE with a KL-divergence quality indicator for bolt looseness signals; shown to improve diagnosis accuracy, no other sampler named.
Own physics-inspired conditional latent diffusion model synthesizes rare PV defect samples; multi-task classification plus segmentation; whole framework compared with other systems only.
KD-SMOTE, an extended oversampler that considers relevant activities, plus a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM; F1 reported on assembly data, no sampler comparison stated.
Outlier-SMOTE allocates more synthesis to minority points far from the others; compared with traditional SMOTE on five benchmark sets and a COVID-19 set.

Hierarchical clustering guides oversampling within minority sub-clusters before a parallel MapReduce SVM; abstract does not say whether new samples are synthetic; comparison methods unnamed. Multi-label.
Conditional GAN with no stated change generates minority attack samples; GAN-based algorithm is the titled proposal; reported superior to existing oversampling methods on UNSW-NB15.
AE-OM: autoencoder trained on the majority manifold reconstructs new minority samples; compared with 15 popular imbalance methods.
GraphSGN synthesizes minority nodes with feature mixing and class-balanced graph augmentation; beats competitive baselines, presumably other graph oversamplers, on six graph sets.
DTWSSE: SMOTE-style oversampling for time series with DTW distance and interpolation in a siamese autoencoder space; improves downstream model, no other sampler named.
DEC-SVM: differential evolution mutation and crossover oversampling followed by clustering-based cleaning; compared with SMOTE-SVM and DE-SVM on ten UCI sets.
Own transformer-based conditional WGAN synthesizes fault samples, reinforcement learning selects good ones; reported to beat recently published methods for AHU fault diagnosis.
Proposed WSEQ-GAN augments imbalanced DNA sequence classes; compared with sampling and SMOTE and with non-augmented data.
Graph-DAO generates synthetic minority nodes before the GNN with sum-product network distribution alignment; claims best results on four graph sets, comparators not named.
Novel resampling strategy raises the weight of hard samples inside an XGBoost ensemble; abstract does not say whether examples are synthetic, duplicated or reweighted. Compared with ensembles only.
End-to-end three-player adversarial oversampling with a mixture of generators, discriminator and multiclass classifier; gains reported over the baseline classifier only.
Physics-aware conditional VAE augments imbalanced failure-mode classes; compared with well-established oversamplers and a non-augmented baseline across eight classifiers.
GAN-based oversampler that keeps only generated minority samples selected by k-NN; outperforms existing methods on F1. Korean journal, full-text language should be checked.
Novel resampling that translates majority samples into minority samples with a translation loss inside a deep ECG model; MIT-BIH results, no sampler comparison stated.
AWGAN: density-based noise removal, boundary-aware weights and weighted GAN generation; compared with six traditional and five GAN-based oversamplers on 21 datasets.
Two novel density-based samplers; the second combines undersampling with oversampling, but the abstract does not say the oversampling is synthetic. Compared with popular algorithms on 16 sets.
Stock trading action model; its designed extrema oversampling gives no sign of synthetic generation and the contribution is the network. Full text could change this.
Proposed GAVAE joins VAE latent learning with adversarial training to generate minority traffic samples; UNSW-NB15 and NSL-KDD; compared only with unspecified traditional methods.
TDGN with its own density-based Wasserstein GAN for synthetic fraud samples plus a time-aware gated network; whole method compared with unnamed competitors.
Model-driven sampling generates new points from an induced probabilistic graphical model; compared with two representative samplers on four medical sets.
Generates tail-class features by sampling calibrated class distributions to train the classifier; long-tail CIFAR-100-LT and mini-ImageNet-LT; state-of-the-art claim, samplers not named.
Empirical defect prediction study on NASA MDP that also proposes SMOTE ASMO as an improvement of SMOTE; evaluation of the variant is only implied.
ADASYN balancing then range-constrained CTGAN generation, named in the title as the scheme; compared with ADASYN alone and with TVAE.
Lung nodule framework with its own multi-kernel over-sampling beside feature selection; G-mean and AUC against competing methods. Synthetic generation not spelled out.
Analyzes the DeepSMOTE penalty term in paper and code versions and proposes a refined penalty; validated on MNIST, FMNIST, CIFAR-10, SVHN. Mostly analysis, small refinement.
Safe-Level SMOTE with a modified KNN function (Manhattan distance) for hyperspectral data, with CNN bagging at differentiated sampling rates; beats other imbalance methods.
AP-iB-SMOTE: improved affinity propagation clustering with Gini impurity plus improved Borderline-SMOTE with separate formulas for safe and risky samples; beats conventional methods on 27 sets.
LAMO: borderline seeds, local distribution and adaptive GMM generation around seeds; compared with state-of-the-art oversamplers on simulated and real data.
SOAR selects minority seeds in deciles D3 to D9 of an anomaly score before synthesis, multiclass; beats baseline and state-of-the-art oversamplers on 17 UCI sets.

Oscillation recognition framework introduces DeepSMOTE1D, oversampling encoder-decoder features, and evaluates its effect; unclear whether it is the paper's own adaptation or existing DeepSMOTE used as is.

IECA: entropy-based removal of low-information instances in overlap regions plus interpolation of high-information defect instances near the boundary; five classifiers, three datasets, no sampler comparison stated.
ESRT generates synthetic minority samples in the embedding space near decision boundaries inside a feature extractor; 21-class cytology data; framework compared with existing methods only.
Develops Three-way Oversampling (3WOS) to generate minority fault-text vectors within a Bayesian network diagnosis pipeline; validated on railway cases, no sampler comparison.
New algorithm combining oversampling with boosting, each round's error guiding the next sampling; beats widely used imbalance methods. Abstract does not say the samples are synthetic.
Deception-risk text framework introducing its own semantic-constrained oversampling beside a wolf search optimizer; compared with GWO and BERT baselines only; generation mechanism not described.
Generates pseudo-fault samples by wavelet phase space reconstruction to balance bearing fault classes, with class-balancing weights; 36 imbalance experiments, no sampler comparison stated.
Hybrid framework with its own noise removal on the majority class feeding a synthetic minority generator; G-mean improvements on eleven datasets, apparently over unprocessed data.
TAMS generates synthetic minority instances restricted to safe-core regions, paired with dynamic cost-sensitive learning; gains reported against standard XGBoost only.
Improved SMOTE with sample-distribution based resampling inside a selective ensemble for ECG heartbeats; MIT-BIH accuracy reported, no sampler comparison stated.
DRCW-ASEG produces synthetic minority examples adaptively during dynamic classifier weighting in a one-vs-one multiclass scheme; experimental study with several base classifiers.
KNNOR identifies critical and safe areas by relative density and generates synthetic minority points; compared with ten contemporary oversamplers.
Adversarial augmentation with a generator, a real-fake discriminator and an auxiliary risk discriminator for high-risk credit samples; three real datasets, comparators not named.
Plain GAN over BERT embeddings generates synthetic spam, named in the title; improvement over traditional techniques, read as conventional resampling. If that reading fails, E1.
Neural network ensemble with negative correlation learning plus a presampling step; compared with no sampling and SMOTE-sampled MLP, but nothing says whether presampling is synthetic.
MBA creates additional defective samples with mutation operators to rebalance defect data; compared with five oversamplers and a baseline on 27 PROMISE releases; mixed results.
Weld flaw classification using SMOTE as it is; the developed part is cross-validated SVM recursive feature elimination.
SMART-SMOTE with noise removal, feature selection, dissimilarity-based neighbor choice and Gaussian noise; beats state-of-the-art methods on two datasets.
PSO-based data balancer for diabetes data, compared with random undersampling and the imbalanced set; abstract does not say whether it generates synthetic examples or selects samples.
GraphAdasyn: density-adaptive multiclass oversampling of minority nodes using hybrid graph views; beats all baseline methods on imbalanced node classification.
Proposes bag-level oversampling for imbalanced multiple instance learning, nine benchmark sets; abstract does not say whether the new bags are synthetic or what it is compared with.
HSDP: data region partition, noise minority removal, boundary seeds and weighted in-cluster synthetic generation; compared with typical sampling methods on eight datasets.
OCH-SMOTE: one-vs-one decomposition with an enhanced CH-SMOTE for multiclass imbalance; compared with classical and state-of-the-art oversamplers on 18 sets.
ClustSyn: clustering plus Mahalanobis-distance synthetic minority generation; compared with AdaBoost, RUSBoost and SMOTEBoost on 11 datasets.
Potato leaf disease study using generic over- and undersampling before random forest, compared with each other and original data; called new but no generator described; focus is features.
DCAES, a deep convolutional autoencoder with SMOTE, generates minority attack samples, followed by DBSCAN undersampling and Tomek links; UNSW-NB15 comparison experiments, comparators not named.
Novel oversampling for NER: DBpedia concepts build GPT-3 prompts that generate examples for under-represented entity classes; benchmark NER sets. Task is sequence labelling, results not stated.
Software release: Shiny web app wrapping 16 existing imbalanced-learn samplers with a diagnostic module for synthetic sample quality; proposes no resampling method of its own.
Oversampling that produces non-dominated synthetic examples under two criteria plus a specialized undersampling step; compared with several leading balancing algorithms using GEP.
Stock conditional GAN proposed for augmenting minority AF signals in an ECG stroke model; compared with other augmentation options including plain oversampling, which it only matched.
Geometric SMOTE places synthetic samples in a hyper-sphere or hyper-spheroid around selected minority instances; compared with SMOTE and baseline methods.
Improved SMOTEBagging: an improved SMOTE combined with selective ensemble and bagging; four UCI sets and protein interaction data, no sampler comparison stated.
CycleGAN applied to generate minority fraud transactions, titled as the contribution, with no stated change to the model; only shown to improve the detector, no other sampler compared.
Proposes DEBOHID, a differential evolution based oversampler; compared with nine oversampling methods on 44 datasets with three classifiers.
Coins SUPERAUG, adaptive multi-noise injection combined with SMOTE with strength tuned by model performance; improvement reported only against unaugmented pipelines.
VAE with mutual information added to its loss generates abnormal-class data before a stacking ensemble; only the whole model is compared with five other models.

Claims embedding-level oversampling in a fused image-metadata space as key contribution, but generation techniques are unnamed and may be existing; only image-only baselines compared. First check kept.
Searched augmentation policies then standard PGGAN generate minority SAR images, presented in title; only gain over the imbalanced baseline reported, no other sampler or generator.
Improved SMOTE: kNN graph and GCN feature-space generation, then AE-GAN regeneration; five imbalanced datasets, says best performance without naming the comparators.
Proposes WMCOA, weighted minority cluster oversampling for within and between class imbalance; compared with several common imbalance processing algorithms on 20 datasets.
Intrusion detection system claiming a novel cluster-based oversampling technique, details not given; only the whole system is compared with existing methods on three datasets.
Proposes data partition hybrid sampling with boundary weighted BMW-SMOTE plus dynamic model selection; whole method compared with typical imbalanced classification methods, samplers not named.
New algorithm resamples per subtree on its feature subset inside random forest (PSRF, PBSRF, PADRF); compared with plain SMOTE, B-SMOTE and ADASYN forests on 10 KEEL sets.
LLM routing model; proposed text augmentation by transformations plus perplexity-based sampling is not clearly minority-class synthesis; no sampler comparison. First check kept; include arguable.
Novel SMOTE-based traffic augmentation algorithm whose hyperparameters are tuned by KS test and ROC AUC validation; F1 gain on CICIDS2017 over the unaugmented baseline only.
Introduces PFS-SMOTE, generating fault samples in a physics-guided Siamese feature space; accuracy on two bearing datasets, no other sampler named in abstract.
Class-wise KDE sampling used as the oversampler without a stated change, named in title; only random forest accuracy reported, no comparison with another sampler.
Proposes Stochastic Sensitivity Oversampling, Gaussian synthetic samples within Q-neighborhoods of minority points; experiments on several datasets, comparators not named.
Proposes GASMOTE: SMOTE then genetic selection, crossover and mutation of samples; average metric gain on 28 datasets, apparently over the unbalanced baseline.
Matrix factorization generator of synthetic positive samples in a subspace with cost-driven counts and distance filtering; compared with AMSCO and other resampling approaches on 10 microbial sets.
Proposes NDESO: noisy points displaced toward neighbors, then random oversampling; 14 alternatives on 20 datasets. New points are shifted originals plus duplicates, so synthetic status is arguable.
Introduces TDCGAN, a triple-discriminator conditional GAN to balance phishing URL data; compared with SMOTE and RandomOverSampler.
Novel hypersphere-based over- and under-sampling inside AdaBoost with a new weighting factor, generating minority samples in hard regions; 28 datasets, comparators not named.
Proposes LoRAS, oversampling from an approximated minority manifold via affine combinations of shadow samples; compared with SMOTE and several SMOTE extensions on 14 datasets.
Random majority downsampling chained with standard SMOTE, claimed as first use at regional level; only classifiers and tumour methods compared, no other sampler.
Claims a novel hybrid of autoencoder and K-means that generates synthetic minority attack data; generator not described, could be existing parts; CICIoT2023, no sampler comparison.
Proposes TSDAS-SMOTE, improved Borderline-SMOTE with two-step filtering and adaptive seed selection; compared with six oversamplers on wind turbine bolt data.
Proposes WASSKIL, a MAHAKIL-based oversampler using Wasserstein distance for partitioning; outperforms MAHAKIL on PHM 2015 plant data.
Proposes K-means Triangular Synthesis generating samples by cluster density, joined to a pinball-loss large margin classifier; comparative experiments, comparators not named.
Introduces KNN-SMOTE, an enhancement of Borderline-SMOTE; better F-score, G-mean and AUC than other methods on five UCI sets. DOCTYPE: chapter
Proposes PAIO, position-aware interpolation for inland, borderline and trapped minority samples, plus GIC for categorical attributes; real datasets, comparators not named.
Method probes the best SMOTE balance ratio jointly with iterative L1-SVM feature selection; compared with unbalanced variants and another balancing method. Mostly feature selection, E1 defensible.
Proposes iBRF, a novel hybrid sampling step inside each bootstrap of a random forest; beats BRF and 14 sampling techniques on 44 datasets. Synthetic generation implied only.
Proposes CDE-SMOTE: SMOTE amount set from the estimated target class distribution in cross-project defect prediction; compared with other CPDP approaches on 14 projects.
Presents SMOTENN, a novel MapReduce resampler doing oversampling and intelligent undersampling in one pass; outperforms alternative resampling techniques.
DiGAN applies a GAN with no stated change to balance diabetes data, with Laplacian score selection; named in title and reported better than SMOTE-based methods.
Borderline-SMOTE samples further optimized by a genetic algorithm, named in title as synthetic sample optimization; only whole Trojan detector compared with existing techniques.
Proposes Improved SMOTE plus Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN with imbalance ratio; the three are compared with each other, judged mainly by class balance achieved.
Develops Re-SSS: safe sample screening to select majority samples plus a weighted SMOTE generating informative minority samples; experiments reported, comparators not named.
Introduces MGS-GRF for mixed features: local-covariance kernel density for continuous, generalized random forest for categorical; compared with SMOTE-NC and other strategies.
Case identification from medical free text; existing under- and oversampling and cost-sensitive learning used to vary imbalance ratio; only a baseline classifier compared.
Classifier-feedback-guided sampling from a text-to-image model to add synthetic images for underrepresented classes; state of the art with fewer generated samples on ImageNet-LT.
Proposes ISMOTE, random interpolation in the ball around a minority instance and its neighbor; beats SMOTE and no resampling. Full-text language of this journal needs checking.
Proposes NC_Link_MWMOTE, MWMOTE with NC_Link hierarchical clustering; outperforms a baseline method on six datasets by F1 and AUC.
Proposes genetic algorithms that set sampling ratios for existing over-, under- and hybrid samplers; beats the same samplers with random ratios on 14 datasets. No new generator.
Proposes FRDOAC: affinity propagation, fuzzy representativeness difference as imbalance metric, chromosome-inheritance generation; better than other imbalance algorithms on 16 datasets.
Introduces conformational oversampling: extra molecule conformations generated to balance toxic class on Tox21; authors say samples are not artificial, so synthetic status is arguable.
Density-weighted cGAN with noise removal and separate generation for boundary and safe regions on stroke data; beats SMOTE, ADASYN and Borderline-SMOTE.
Proposes MLNaNBDOS, a multi-label natural-neighbor boundary oversampler with adaptive oversampling factor; nine benchmark methods on three load deviation datasets.
Introduces elk herd optimization to find SMOTE sampling rates (AEHO-based SMOTE) for ToN-IoT intrusion data with BiLSTM; no sampler comparison. Standard SMOTE with tuned rate, E1 arguable.
Novel dynamic SMOTE-based rotation forest: per-tree balancing mixing resampled and SMOTE-generated minority instances at a changing rate; beats popular sampling methods on three hyperspectral sets.
Improved VAE-CGAN oversampler with density-peak clustering noise filter and modified Wasserstein loss; compared with 5 classical oversamplers on 10 datasets.
Novel oversampling technique placing new samples by intra-class and inter-class distance matrices for multiclass data; outperforms common oversampling techniques on 14 datasets.
Novel MOSGNN built on oversampled minority graphs at subgraph, graph and pairwise scales; beats five models on 16 datasets. Whether oversampled graphs are synthetic is not stated.
Proposes Gaussian noise upsampling as a novel imbalance correction for radiomics recurrence models; compared with seven conventional correction methods and no correction.
Proposes FLO: focal-loss Lasso feature selection, then a focal-loss-based oversampler generating minority instances; high-dimensional biomedical datasets, comparators not named.
Neuro-symbolic ECG arrhythmia framework; generic augmentation-based oversampling is one listed component with no stated change and no sampler comparison.
Random forest versus XGBoost for stunting; minority data drawn by simple quartile-based random sampling as a preprocessing step, not proposed or compared as a method.
Proposes GASMOTE: a genetic algorithm sets per-sample sampling rates for SMOTE; beats SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE on 10 datasets, applied to rockburst data.
Power system security assessment model that also proposes an improved adaptive synthetic sampling algorithm, details not given; tested on 39-bus and 118-bus systems, no sampler comparison.
Borderline-SMOTE used as it is before AdaBoost for a hysterectomy decision model; only compared with conventional classifiers.
Proposes MAOTE, an adaptive evolutionary-search oversampler with classifier feedback inside multi-layer LSSVM for multi-class faults; beats ten data augmentation methods.
Proposes an inception-based GAN to synthesize heart sounds for underrepresented classes; compared only with and without GAN. If the GAN is standard this would be E1.
AutoML framework that picks among 12 existing samplers, losses and calibration by Bayesian optimization; SVMSMOTE selected. No new generator; include arguable as changed application.
Proposes a weight decision algorithm setting how many samples to generate from each minority sample via edge-detection gradients; several imbalanced datasets, no comparison result stated.
Random undersampling followed by routine image augmentation as data curation; contribution is the fine-tuned EfficientNet comparison, no sampler comparison. DOCTYPE: chapter
Pretrained diffusion model with standard LoRA fine-tuning generates rare-class images, proposed as the pipeline; compared only with training on real data alone.
Proposes Anch-SCGAN, an anchor-based conditional GAN with contrastive generator loss for tabular oversampling; outperforms known imbalanced learning methods on 16 datasets.
Proposes chaoticGAN with chaotic noise input for minority oversampling, plus hybrid with OCSVM undersampling; compared with GAN, WGAN and CTGAN.
Besides a random forest sgRNA classifier, proposes a new method called CS-Smote, mechanism not described; only the predictor is compared with other predictors.
Proposes GAN-based oversampling (GBO) and SVM-SMOTE-GAN (SSG); both beat original SMOTE on eight benchmark datasets. Preprint.
Proposes HSMOTE, a SMOTE-inspired module generating synthetic vertices and their hyperedge correlations for tail classes; whole framework compared on Amazon-LT.
Enhances ADASYN with decision-boundary proximity and realistic distribution constraints for Ponzi contract detection; whole approach compared with other detectors on XBlock.
Fraud detection method with its own kernel-guided adversarial module generating synthetic samples, inside federated reinforcement learning; whole system beats eight baselines.
Proposes generating synthetic samples in language-model embedding space to upsample minority classes, using unnamed techniques that may be existing oversamplers; no comparison. First check kept.
Proposes alpha-Distance Borderline-ADASYN-SMOTE combining optimized Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN with neighbor distance; applied to ADNI data with DenseNet, no sampler comparison stated.
Proposes DCIA, inserting and adjusting new prototypes for every class in multiclass imbalanced data; synthetic points of its own, but it is instance reduction, not minority oversampling.
Compares existing oversampling, undersampling and combined sampling with wrapper feature selection across classifiers on RT IoT 2022; no resampler of its own.
Proposes VCOS, a synergistic oversampler generating samples guided by classifier performance without repeated training; several real binary datasets, comparators not named.
Proposes NCLO-SMOTE: adaptive clustering of the minority class, overlap cleaning by a Newton cooling rule and cluster-weighted oversampling; ten sampling methods on 48 datasets.
Proposes Data Center Interpolation oversampling inside an ensemble with sparrow-search tuned random forest; whole model compared with other well-known approaches.
Proposes EC-EBO: constrained clustering, entropy-balanced generation regions, hill-climbing placement and entropy-weighted allocation; beats ten oversampling techniques on 60 datasets.
Proposes OHSEC: density-peak-guided under- and oversampling with optimized imbalance ratios and evidence fusion; whole method beats eleven methods. Synthetic points not stated explicitly.
Proposes an algorithm built on a SMOTE variant combined with different error costs for SVM; compared with SMOTE, the cost method, undersampling and regular SVM.
Open RAN conflict management framework; standard SMOTE added to a GNN classifier and compared with GNN without it. GenC generates whole datasets, not minority examples.
Proposes a bias-correction procedure for classifiers trained on synthetic oversampled data such as SMOTE, with bounds and real data analyses; changes use of oversampling, no generator.
Proposes RQSP-SMOTE: regular quadrilateral scoring with perturbation selects samples for multi-linear interpolation without kNN; compared with other improved SMOTE algorithms.
Proposes a parametric method estimating minority class statistics from nearby classes as an alternative to convex-combination oversampling; synthetic and real benchmarks, comparators not named.
Proposes Naive Bayes Sampling, new minority instances by bootstrapping per-feature values; superior to studied approaches including SMOTE on four UCI sets and a medical set. DOCTYPE: thesis
Proposes oversampling by K-means clustering of the minority class and genetic crossover within clusters; KNN and SVM tests. Chinese journal, full-text language needs checking.
Proposes enhanced SMOTE guided by clustering and PCA, plus PPO-guided augmentation and DQN sampling; reports minority recall gains against an unstated baseline. Poorly written abstract.
K-means SMOTE then distance-based undersampling used as steps before an ABC-optimized OS-ELM; contribution is the diagnosis model; compared only with other algorithms, not samplers.
LLM-guided GAN generating new attack patterns, plus standard SMOTE, inside a federated IDS; ablation against configurations without LLM guidance on three IDS datasets.
XGBoost complication model; unnamed oversampling used as preprocessing, synthetic or not is not stated; no own resampler, so exclusion holds either way.
Round-trip translation oversampling plus random undersampling for SemEval intimacy scoring, judged by Pearson r; regression only, no sampler comparison reported.
Claims an enhanced SMOTE with reverse kNN noise removal and density-based allocation; beats SMOTE and original data. Closely resembles published SMOTE-RkNN, novelty to be checked.
Centroid-based oversampling with attribute selection and kNN called the proposed algorithm, compared with traditional oversampling; wording does not show whether the sampler itself is new.
Extends the deep over-sampling framework with weak abstract labels to guide representation; abstract does not say synthetic examples are generated; no sampler comparison named. Preprint.
Plain GAN and WGAN augmentation for a 1D CNN, stressed as the approach; only contrast is SMOTE plus classical models versus GAN plus CNN, a whole-pipeline comparison.
Proposes ASMOBD, density-based adaptive synthesis per minority sample with smoothing, joined with cost-sensitive SVM; beats state-of-art approaches on nine UCI datasets.
Proposes RAMGANH: range-based association rule undersampling with a modified tabular GAN oversampler; SVM on standard datasets, better than other state-of-the-art methods.
Proposes GDO: probabilistic anchor selection by density and distance, Gaussian generation; compared with seven imbalanced learning approaches on 40 KEEL and 10 UCI sets.
Standard GMM sampling of fracture samples named in title and proposal with an iTransformer-LSTM; abstract reports no comparison with any other sampler or generator.
Proposes ILMNN: metric-learned latent space, sample weights and KL safeguard changing how oversampling is applied; comparative experiments but comparators not named; generation step vague.
Designs a dynamic GAN to generate minority samples, with a self-adaptive multilayer ELM; four biomedical datasets, compared with SMOTE-ELM, W-ELM and H-ELM.
Proposes a new SMOTE-based sampling strategy with Relief-based feature selection and random forest; six benchmark and two application datasets, compared with SMOTE.
Proposes three-way decision key sample selection (CTD) and its ensemble (CTDE) feeding SMOTE; superior to comparison and state-of-the-art methods on 10 datasets.
Proposes USWAVG-BS: HVDM noise identification, undersampling or relabeling, then weighted generation; beats 3 undersamplers, 7 oversamplers and 4 hybrids on 10 datasets.
Clinical risk model trying six existing imbalance strategies across eight learners; final model uses random oversampling, duplication only; no resampler of its own.

Original model synthesizing samples in critical areas of the class distribution, set against existing balancing methods; Iris and wine sets. Abstract partly Ukrainian, full-text language needs checking.
Proposes CASS: GMM subcluster centers, proximity-density weights, tailored synthesis; beats nine common sampling algorithms on PHM2010 and an own tool dataset.
Proposes BO-SMOTE: minority samples generated iteratively by Bayesian optimization in targeted intervals with sample selection; beats state-of-the-art oversamplers on twenty datasets.
Develops a sliding-window SMOTE that keeps temporal dependencies, within a drilling condition method; 14 wells; compared only with other network models, not samplers.
Visual analytics tool letting users steer existing under- and oversampling by instance hardness; no generator of its own stated, shown by usage scenario; changed-application reading is arguable.
Proposes a hybrid probabilistic oversampling with sparse group lasso feature selection for Alzheimer diagnosis; whole method compared with baseline and state-of-the-art, generator details absent.
Proposed hybrid: star-topology SMOTE for the minority plus own distribution-based removal of majority instances; biometric data, improvement stated without a named comparator.
Proposes a class distribution alignment technique for imbalanced medical images; abstract gives no basis to tell synthetic generation from reweighting or resampling; baselines unnamed.
Develops multi-kernel over-sampling (MKOS) generating synthetic instances in a learned kernel space, with MKMFA reduction; ADNI; whole method beats unnamed comparable methods.
Proposes LDAS: local density, new cleaning of overlapping majority examples, weighted generation in safe and border areas; KEEL experiments, no comparator named in abstract.
Own dual attention Wasserstein GAN for minority fault synthesis, combined with SMOTE-Tomek, in a fuel cell diagnosis framework; whole framework beats state-of-the-art methods.
Proposes GMO-AC: GMM-based minority generation with Mahalanobis outlier filtering and class overlap weighting; compared with SMOTE and other methods on synthetic and benchmark data.

FoDiKAN: fold-local class-conditional diffusion with anchored DDIM sampling and geometry-aware screening for minority samples; 25 microarray sets; compared with no-synthesis variants and reference baselines.
Proposes CCR-GSVM: majority noise filtering through SVM and GSVM-RU boundaries, then CCR-based boundary generation; comparative experiments on 12 imbalanced datasets.
Proposes VMSG, OC-SVM guided volunteer selection and synthetic minority fault generation with a new loss; beats SMOTE, its variants, GANs and VAEs on ASHRAE data.
Proposes A-RDBOTE: reverse kNN noise removal, minority clustering, representative anchors and generation around them; beats eight oversampling methods on credit-scoring data.
Presents Region-SMOTE: vote rule splitting minority into safe, intermediate and dangerous samples with different handling; four datasets; better performance claimed, comparator not named.
Proposes SMOTE-ADC: SMOTE generation with a weighted eigenvalue distance matrix plus quality checks of generated signals; only generated versus original data is reported.
Contribution is the CardioViT CNN-Transformer architecture; synthetic minority oversampling with feature-space augmentation is only used to validate it under imbalance.
Standard easy data augmentation applied as oversampling for threat-report text classes, presented as the method; only compared with the TRAM baseline and earlier studies, no other sampler.
Own conditional GAN pipeline with spectral normalization, self-attention, multi-metric quality gate and sample weighting for rare tumor MRI classes; recall and AUC gains over an unnamed baseline.
Introduces Quantum-SMOTEV2: swap tests and quantum rotation around one centroid with angular outliers; set against the original Quantum-SMOTE on a telecom churn dataset. Preprint.
Hybrid preprocessing with a new Proximity-Driven Undersampling combined with SMOTE inside a multi-label Hoeffding tree forest; AI4I 2020; whole framework compared with state-of-the-art.
Presents Image-based SMOTified-GAN, an image adaptation of the SMOTE plus GAN oversampler for TB chest X-rays; beats other oversampling techniques with GoogleNet.
Integrates a K* entropy distance into SMOTE and CNN plus Tomek links, and introduces SMOTE plus SMaRT; improves on the earlier SMOTE+VDM with random undersampling.
GAN oversampling followed by a novel adaptive neighborhood weighted undersampling that removes generated and majority instances; beats benchmark methods on artificial and customer datasets.
Claims a custom oversampling strategy for liver-injury prediction and reports gains; abstract does not say how examples are made or whether they are synthetic. Preprint.
Readmission prediction with tree, forest and rule classifiers; abstract mentions no resampling or synthetic examples at all.
Proposes MC-NRO, multiclass neighborhood repartition oversampling using mutual class potential with cleaning for label noise; outperforms other advanced oversampling strategies.

DySMOTE approach: SMOTE oversampling with per-epoch dynamic sample selection in MLP training, called the proposed approach; EEG of eight subjects; beats unnamed existing methods. May be a prior method.
Novel augmentation adversarially perturbing autoencoder latent vectors, framed for imbalanced time series; abstract does not say only minority classes are augmented or name comparators.
Proposes diversity-based multi-cluster oversampling using Mahalanobis distance and cluster density for defect prediction; five learners; lower false alarm rate, comparator not named.
Coins conformational oversampling: generated molecule conformations as new examples to balance toxicity classes; Tox21, balanced accuracy gain reported without any other sampler.
Develops a 1-D DCGAN augmentation framework generating radar range profiles for minority classes; outperforms state-of-the-art oversampling methods.
Develops Expansive Over-Sampling: convex combinations of minority samples and nearest adversaries in CNN embedding space, in a three-phase framework; beats cost-sensitive and resampling methods.
Compares GLMM Tree and GMERF on poverty data; unnamed oversampling applied, with versus without only; no own resampler, so exclusion holds either way.

Develops a 3D conditional latent diffusion model with attention modules generating class-conditioned MRI against scarcity and imbalance; classifier trained on synthetic, tested on real; no comparator.
Presents SI-SMOTE, sample-information based SMOTE using Mahalanobis distance, inside a semi-supervised tri-training ensemble; bearing and wheel data; whole method beats unnamed other methods.
Presents a hybrid ensemble integrating undersampling and oversampling with Bagging and AdaBoost, within a comparative study of resampling; oversampler type, synthetic or not, is not stated.
Proposes Informative Sample Selection of minority seeds for synthetic generation; 22 datasets, better than SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN, safe-level SMOTE and ROS.
Fraud pipeline of autoencoder features, weighted voting and ESMOTE-GAN, an already published oversampler that is employed as is; compared only across classifiers.
Proposes HNaNSMOTE, parameter-free hybrid natural neighbor rule for SMOTE generation; 32 datasets, three classifiers, beats state-of-the-art oversampling techniques.
Claims GraphBalance: minority nodes synthesized in an embedding space with a trained edge generator; three datasets, unnamed baselines. Abstract mirrors GraphSMOTE, check for derivative.
SMOTE-ENN chained with LOF named in the title as hybrid balancing for a two-tier IIoT IDS; abstract reports no comparison with any other sampler.
Proposes M-D2GAN, a mixed dual discriminator GAN generating mixed-type minority fault samples; train braking case study, better than classic GAN on F-measure and G-mean.
Proposes MTDOT, multi-level back-translation through several languages to create new offensive-class text; HASOC21; compared with single-level back-translation and with SMOTE.
Proposes FG-SMOTE, fuzzy-based Gaussian SMOTE with a fuzzy Levenshtein distance; evaluated with a deep belief network, scores given without a comparator.
Proposes SSAO: GMM clustering of each minority class and generation inside enclosing spheres for multi-class data; 15 datasets, compared with 11 resampling algorithms.
Proposes NB-MIO: two-stage Tomek link search to clean boundary majority samples and pick safe minority seeds; 17 benchmarks against 15 methods, top Friedman rank.
Proposes DAFL: KS drift test, dynamic SMOTE and adaptive client weighting built into federated learning; fraud and UNSW data; compared with unnamed baseline methods, not samplers.
Proposes FC-SMOTE, fuzzy clustering based SMOTE for multiclass voice pathology data; outperforms traditional oversampling algorithms on MEEI and SVD.
Novel generation of synthetic attack samples merging frequent itemset mining with a generative model, for class imbalance; checked against original data and with three classifiers.
Own scheme: SHAP feature selection, minority instances mapped by t-SNE to a latent space, synthetic samples by Gaussian noise sampling; three botnet sets, no sampler comparison.
Customized diffusion model (CDDPM) generates fault samples against imbalance, used unlabeled in self-supervised pretraining; HVAC diagnosis; whole framework beats state-of-the-art baselines.
Eigen-Entropy metric with two EE-guided oversampling techniques that beat reported literature methods on 10 sets; abstract does not say whether samples are synthetic or selected.
Proposes GAN-AHR, choosing CGAN or Borderline-SMOTE per class by compactness and density; NF-UNSW-NB15 with random forest; improvement reported without a named comparator.
Proposes RBM-SMOTE: a restricted Boltzmann machine transforms SMOTE examples toward the true distribution; one credit scoring experiment, comparator not stated.
Introduces QI-SMOTE, quantum-inspired synthetic oversampling; MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV mortality; compared with Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN, SMOTE-ENN, SMOTE-Tomek and SVM-SMOTE. Preprint.
Proposes CorrOV-CSEn: correlation-based oversampling with custom rate and zone inside cost-sensitive AdaBoost; 8 datasets against 13 state-of-the-art methods.
Proposes genetic-algorithm oversampling with Gaussian initial population and Euclidean fitness selection, classified by DNN; outperforms data generated by SMOTE and ADASYN.
Compares existing attack technique extraction methods; an unnamed oversampling strategy is tried as mitigation, with versus without only; no own resampler. Preprint.
Designs ITCGAN, a GAN with classifier and pretraining module generating minority traffic samples end to end; ISCXVPN2016, surpasses five state-of-the-art oversampling methods.
Proposes a SMOTE scheme with K-means and intuitionistic fuzzy weights for seeds, paired with quadratic surface SVM; artificial and real sets with label noise, comparator not named.
Proposes CSMOTE: variational encoding into private and common Gaussian latent spaces to generate minority time series; five benchmarks, beats other oversampling baselines in most cases.
Proposes SB-GAN: conditional GAN with adaptive class balancing scaled to the smallest class for hyperspectral classes; three public scenes, accuracy reported without a comparator.

Proposes an artificial immune network combined with an improved SMOTE to generate samples, inside robust Relief-F feature selection; six medical sets; compared with feature selection methods only. Preprint.
Generates minority data by single-point crossover, then Jellyfish Search selects an optimal subset; 18 datasets, compared with famous oversampling methods and ACOR.
Improves SMOTE and combines it with K-means and random undersampling for IPTV complaint prediction; performs better than Borderline-SMOTE with Naive Bayes.
